title: Jifeng Bookstore Opens Its First Branch, in Jinan: "A Salute to All Who Cherish the Humanities and Science" | Stories of 2017 ⑮
excerpt: "I think what we're doing is genuinely worthwhile. This society needs some dissenting voices, needs some free space. And if you're lucky enough to have the chance to be part of that — I think that is a kind of meaning for my life."
body:
"I think what we're doing is genuinely worthwhile. This society needs some dissenting voices, needs some free space. And if you're lucky enough to have the chance to be part of that — I think that is a kind of meaning for my life."

On December 16, Qu Xiangdong, chairman of Xingzhi Exploration, got a WeChat message from his friend Gao Junling: unless he could answer the question at the front door — "e^(πi)+1=？" — he wouldn't be let in. Qu had studied Chinese literature. "I had no idea what that formula was," he said. "I was terrified." So he "snuck in through the back door."

Qu had come for the opening of Jifeng Bookstore's Jinan branch — the first outpost the famous Shanghai independent bookstore has opened outside the city. Gao Junling is the new branch's general manager.

By two in the afternoon, the event space, more than a hundred square meters, was packed, people sitting and standing, all waiting quietly for the ceremony to begin. Among them were longtime Jifeng readers, some of whom had traveled in specially from Shanghai; classmates, friends, and family of Jifeng general manager Yu Miao; and a number of writers and scholars.

Yu Miao hosted the ceremony, and from the podium he restated his view of what Jifeng is. "What we are taking part in is not a purely commercial project. Our bookstore is a bookstore with a human touch, because it cares about people's wellbeing, their right to think, their dignity, and their longing for a good life. And the bookstore is more than a bookstore — it is also a cultural space. Here, people meet one another, and ideas collide with ideas. Of course, right now, anything to do with ideas carries risk. Whether you are willing to take that risk is each person's own choice," Yu said.

After his brief remarks, Yu introduced the guests one by one and asked them to speak. They included Jifeng founder Yan Bofei; writer Liu Yawei; economist Wen Kejian; military-strategy scholar Zhao Chu; Feng Keli, editor-in-chief of 《老照片》 (*Old Photographs*) at Shandong Pictorial Press; Liu Gengzi, a Shandong University board member and adjunct professor; and others.

"To be honest, my feelings today are a little mixed. Two things are happening to us at once, arriving almost back to back — the birth of a new bookstore and the coming death of one that has held on for twenty years. So birth and death are being stitched together, head to tail, within the span of barely a month." Yan Bofei told the room.

![Gao Junling (left) and Yan Bofei (right). Photo: Jifeng Bookstore](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171218200943U6quwb4HN2mpkaxB.jpg-w600)

### A New Jifeng With a Strong Scientific Streak

The newborn Jinan branch's most distinctive feature, compared with Jifeng Shanghai, is a new "Jifeng Science" section that puts science at the front of the store.

As mentioned above, the scientific mood greets you the moment you reach the front door. Above the entrance are the words "A Salute to Euler," and the question "e^(πi)+1=？" comes straight from Euler's identity. Climb a staircase lined on both sides with books to the second floor, and you face a black wall holding a matrix of 49 clocks. Gao Junling explained: "I worked it out — since the Big Bang, the universe has cooled for roughly 10^17 seconds, and the combinations of time on this wall add up to about 10^49 seconds."

To the left of the black wall is a book area of more than 400 square meters, holding roughly 60,000 titles and a small selection of cultural merchandise. The categories cover not only the large body of humanities and social-science scholarship that is Jifeng's signature, but also plenty of science books, children's books, and young-adult titles — there is even an Amazon Kindle corner. To the right of the black wall is a café of more than 200 square meters, which has partnered with Mobike. That is why the Jinan branch has been called something of the "world's first Mobike-themed bookstore." Between the books and the café sits an event area of more than 100 square meters. The store covers 850 square meters in all, a little smaller than the Shanghai flagship's 1,100-plus.

![The front entrance of Jifeng Bookstore Jinan. Photo: Weibo @小岛书店在蓬莱](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/201712182010518qcDTW36nwGVxY75.jpg-w600)

![The front entrance of Jifeng Bookstore Jinan. Photo: Weibo @小岛书店在蓬莱](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171218201059npBFuGjPR0saTW4h.jpg-w600)

Beyond that, Jifeng Jinan has teamed up with the Shanghai STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) Cloud Center to set up the "Jifeng Science® & Jinan STEM Lab," which will run a series of science-education courses for young people.

More important, to fit the Jinan branch's overall tone, its tagline has changed from Shanghai Jifeng's "An independent cultural stance, free expression of thought" to "A salute to all who cherish the humanities and science."

On that change, Feng Keli told us in an interview: "I think folding science in may be a deliberate move — a way to soften, just a little, the sharp edge the humanities brand used to carry. (Of course,) putting science forward as a guiding idea for a bookstore is also a very important thing that society needs. So in that sense it's not just softening — it's also innovation."

Yan Bofei, Yu Miao, and Gao Junling, though, all stress the organic link between Jifeng and science. Yan Bofei said: "Back then, after the whole revolutionary utopia collapsed, there was a stretch of real disorientation. In that disorientation, we needed to find a new spiritual benchmark for ourselves. For me, what I sought was science. This new, reliable thing didn't claim to be the ultimate truth. It had no such grand ambition — it was empirical, but also certain."

![Jifeng Bookstore Jinan. Photo: Jifeng Bookstore](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171218201511UGO7qtXJkBY5jflb.jpg-w600)

![Jifeng Bookstore Jinan. Photo: Jifeng Bookstore](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171218201521FjtszgPAuSYqCnoM.jpg-w600)

Yu Miao and Gao Junling, for their part, note that they both studied engineering and the natural sciences and have always felt at home with science. They also admire STEM education and want it to be a defining feature of Jifeng Jinan. Yu said: "The humanities and science are inseparable. Science, at bottom, first needs the free thinking of the humanities — that space for free thought and the capacity to think — before it can move forward. I feel the two fit together beautifully." Gao Junling sees it the same way: at their roots, both the humanities and science are a pursuit of logic and a pursuit of truth.

Neither of them accepts that proposing science was a way to "soften the sharp edge." They see it as "natural," "a logical next step," something they "didn't think too hard about." This owes a great deal to the two teams' different strengths.

"The Shanghai Jifeng team is deeply versed in literature, history, and philosophy — it's a team of master's and doctoral graduates. The Jinan side will be a bit different, because among the staff here there tend to be more people from science and engineering," Yu Miao told QDaily.

So the book selection for Jifeng Jinan is handled entirely by the Shanghai team, "but it will be a little less academic than Shanghai's — a little closer to a general readership," Yu added. The Jinan team will concentrate on science books and science-training courses, which will "become the focus of Jifeng Jinan's efforts."

![Jifeng Bookstore Jinan. Photo: Jifeng Bookstore](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171218201620wqGZh5RTgDb4UikH.jpg-w600)

![Jifeng Bookstore Jinan. Photo: Jifeng Bookstore](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/201712182016287jI42dGOJMT5nkmF.jpg-w600)

Gao Junling leads the Jinan branch's team of more than twenty, and he is Yu Miao's old classmate. After finishing his master's at Shandong University, he spent years at Shandong Telecom in technical development. He later started his own company, handed its management to others, and freed up much of his time.

In 2015, Yu Miao came to him, hoping he could help scout sites for Jifeng's new branch. At the time, Yu felt a new store would let Jifeng reach more readers, realize his vision of turning the bookstore into a true public space, and ease some of the financial pressure on the store — so he had been pushing on it every way he could.

In Shanghai, they discussed several possible deals — including sites at Fuxing Park on Huaihai Middle Road, Xinjiangwan, Pudong's Balitai, and Jiading District — but all of them were called off, for one reason or another.

For a store outside Shanghai, Yu Miao and his team set their sights on cities along the Beijing–Shanghai corridor. Gao Junling spent more than a year on the road, "visiting nearly every major mall along the Beijing–Shanghai line," but most fell through over rent. Then, by chance, Gao learned that Jinan's Ronghui Old Commercial Port was looking for tenants — a commercial real-estate project funded by Hong Kong's Ronghui Group and developed by Shandong Ronghui Real Estate.

"One look and I felt it had a lot in common with Shanghai. This area was also a foreign concession, with similar architecture. At the same time, it's a place China opened on its own initiative — it has a certain historical depth. Opening here is more true to Jifeng's values than opening in a typical CBD business district. The building is nice too, and the local leasing team gave us very good terms — basically rent-free. And I'm a Jinan native myself, so I decided this would be the first branch after Shanghai." Gao Junling told QDaily.

![Jifeng Bookstore Jinan. Photo: QDaily](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171218202803Wy62UhrJvqPfTLYw.jpg-w600)

![Jifeng Bookstore Jinan. Photo: QDaily](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171218202817U9WxgQiDRrd5Kwat.jpg-w600)

### The Original Is About to Close

At the opening ceremony, Yan Bofei raised the question of Jifeng's life and death. Yu Miao answered: "At first I deliberately avoided the subject. Because I feel Shanghai Jifeng has its own way of doing things, its own fate. I didn't want the situation in Shanghai to cast a shadow over Jifeng Jinan. I want Jifeng Jinan to make a fresh start through its own independent operations, and to win the hearts of Jinan's readers."

Shanghai Jifeng's closing date is set for January 31, 2018. The reason is that the landlord, Shanghai Library, declined to renew. The official explanation has not changed: "To prevent the loss of state-owned assets, and in keeping with this institution's current space use and operational needs, the premises will be reclaimed for internal use."

"Earlier closures were down to the business climate, or rent, or operating conditions — but none of that applies this time. Our bookstore's operations have no problems whatsoever, and there are no financial issues. I honestly don't know how to explain it, or what it really has to do with." Yu Miao said in an interview with QDaily on April 23, 2017.

That day, at the unveiling of the farewell ceremony, Yu also said: "We only hope to say goodbye to Shanghai, and to the world, with a composed heart and a graceful bearing."

Over those two hundred-plus days of the countdown, Shanghai Jifeng staged a string of events, and many scholars and readers came to show support and pay their respects.

The events included "Dark Poetry Evening," "Book Theft," "Ezra Vogel: The Course and Key Tensions of China-Japan Relations," "Shi Yongqin: Returning to History's Turning Point — Commemorating the 100th Anniversary of the October Revolution," "Sun Longji: The Past and Present of the Silk Road," and more.

Each day, a poem went up on Jifeng's WeChat official account — for instance: "Bearing this scorching wound, like a firefly keeping its own flame alight | Jifeng Countdown: 46 Days"; "The same desert, the same night, I open my weary eyes again beneath the silvery starlight | Jifeng Countdown: 47 Days"; "You wait outside the dream, to carry my words to those who must stay awake | Jifeng Countdown: 48 Days" — and so on.

![Yu Miao at Shanghai Jifeng Bookstore on April 23, 2017. Photo: Jifeng Bookstore WeChat official account](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/201712182020004HgTv5LKfuJsxleX.jpg-w600)

December 16 — the day Jifeng Jinan opened — was Day 46 of Shanghai's "Jifeng Countdown."

Yu Miao felt that after April, people had gradually reached a shared understanding, all hoping to take part in some way. "I've been planning a huge number of events, because with so little time left, you naturally want to make the most of it. We also hope that in these final days, we stand the last watch, and express more fully our faith in the bookstore and the space, and what they mean — and, for ourselves, mark this last stretch." Yu said.

Feng Keli and Liu Gengzi had both appeared as guests at Shanghai Jifeng before. Together with another Feng Keli (a professor in the School of Political Science and Public Administration at Shandong University and a translator), on October 29, 2016, they held a book talk titled "Personal Memory in a Grand Era — Liu Kemu's 《七千里流亡》 (*Seven Thousand Li of Exile*)." Liu Kemu (1920–2007) was a middle-school student who fled from Shandong to Sichuan during the War of Resistance; Liu Gengzi is his son.

Although Liu Gengzi had heard of Jifeng Bookstore as early as around 2000, that was his first visit in person. He found it very well done, "intellectually very strong," and said "I believe it has shaped many people in Shanghai too." "That Shanghai Jifeng has had to close leaves us feeling helpless, sorry, and sad. Because after all, from Yan Bofei to Yu Miao, twenty years of effort — their passion, their spirit — is truly admirable. A bookstore that built such intellectual depth and cultural atmosphere, as China's social climate shifted and certain very harmful outside forces pressed on it, has had no choice but to drift in those currents. Nothing can be done." Liu Gengzi said with feeling.

![](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171218202227dOvEKL3QI0sCRXba.jpg-w600)

Feng Keli had known Jifeng even longer than Liu Gengzi. Shanghai Jifeng was among the first bookstores to stock 《老照片》 (*Old Photographs*), and was founded around the time the journal began publishing. Through his work, he had a great deal of contact with Jifeng and with Yan Bofei, becoming friends, and later helping them review manuscripts.

When he learned Shanghai Jifeng was closing, Feng Keli, too, felt "saddened" and thought it a great "shame." Looking back over the bookstore's twenty years, Feng — as a publisher — had much to say: "From the late 1990s through the early 2000s, the operating climate for China's publishing and cultural industries was relatively relaxed. That Jifeng could build itself up to that scale has everything to do with that broader social environment. What's happening now reflects the climate of China's whole public-discourse environment. As the saying goes, 'the ducks are first to feel the warmth of the spring river' — and those ducks are people in our line of work: publishers, bookstores. In the business of books, you feel the temperature of the water most keenly. For these twenty years we've been taking in the cold and the warmth, bit by bit."

Those two hundred-plus days also shifted how Yu Miao understood and felt about the bookstore — "more reflection." "Why did all this happen? The principles we've held to — why can't they simply move freely in this society, in this moment? Looking back from here, you realize how important, and how hard, this store's founding motto was from the very start: 'An independent cultural stance, free expression of thought.' Twenty years on, it is still hard. So your understanding of many social phenomena, of the bookstore's founding principles, of the common ground we've been trying to reach with readers — all of it becomes more real, or deeper. These things matter enormously. These things are only just beginning." Yu Miao said.

![Jifeng Bookstore Jinan. Photo: Jifeng Bookstore](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171218202925qd12ElPLVy7ChKIJ.jpg-w600)

![Jifeng Bookstore Jinan. Photo: Jifeng Bookstore](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171218202940uFD7HBwa9ivKsVmU.jpg-w600)

### The Future — Hard to Say

On the day of the opening, Yu Miao was in high spirits, greeting familiar guests and now and then refilling his own glass and drinking. Our interview was done while he drank.

But about Jifeng Jinan's future, Yu Miao has far more to worry about. "First, that it can simply survive normally, without too much interference from non-market forces. That is critically important. Second, in purely commercial terms, if within some period it can become self-sustaining, that would be an even better outcome," Yu said.

In purely commercial terms, breaking even will be no small challenge for Jifeng Jinan. First, there is the wider backdrop of online bookstores rising on the back of technology while physical bookstores decline, and of print books battered by the rise of e-books. Second, Jifeng's business model carries its own limits: Gao Junling says the Jinan branch will center its revenue on selling books and science-course training — which, like Shanghai Jifeng, is a niche market. Third, Jinan is a city of "cultural tradition" and "cultural conservatism." And fourth, Jifeng Jinan's lease runs only five years — and in five years it may well face rising rents and be forced to move or close.

"Commercial real estate today chases profit and doesn't look far ahead. As a commercial tenant, we're bound to be squeezed by them, and held over a barrel later on. At our current scale and influence, we have no bargaining power at all. We also hope — even for government subsidies, or help from like-minded people — to carry us a bit further. And of course we rely on ourselves. That side of things is unknown. There's no commercial plan at all," Gao Junling told QDaily.

![Jifeng Bookstore Jinan. Photo: Jifeng Bookstore](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20171218202734AtX2lRsd36Ik0ZVG.jpg-w600)

Beyond the commercial uncertainty, there is the uncertainty of the social environment. "I think Shanghai and Jinan are in roughly the same kind of social environment. In a broad environment like that, doing what we're trying to do will certainly carry some difficulty. And Jifeng has already built up wide social influence — so what attitude will the cultural environment here take? How much tolerance will let us succeed? That is an open question," Feng Keli said.

Around 2015, Yan Bofei asked Yu Miao — who by then had been running Jifeng Bookstore for about three years — "Have you ever had regrets?"

Yu Miao's answer at the time was: "Not once. Every difficulty was foreseen, but the meaning of what we're doing is greater than any of them."

Two more years passed. Between sips, QDaily asked him the same question again: Have you ever had regrets?

"There are definitely no regrets. All of these problems can be reasoned through and foreseen. I think what we're doing is genuinely worthwhile. This society needs some dissenting voices, needs some free space. And if you're lucky enough to have the chance to be part of that — I think that is a kind of meaning for my life. Because so much of life's meaning is self-assigned. I simply take it as given that this is my life's meaning. And that assumption gives me a great deal of drive." Yu Miao said.

Postscript: e^(πi)+1=0
